name: Car or light truck (gas or diesel)

comps.spec: Heated-seat pads (cushion and back), 12 V, 10–70 W a seat in three steps (Dometic MSH300). The car's controller regulates them (Autopian heated seat): a loose pad needs a fuse and a thermostat or timer. Made to sit on uncovered, not a bed warmer; burns skin that can't feel it
comps.loc: Under the cover of each heated front seat, taped to the foam of cushion and backrest; wiring under the seat

comps.spec: Blade fuses, dozens per car, plus fuse boxes
comps.loc: Under the dash and in the engine bay

notes: Heated-seat pads run on 12 V at 10–70 W a seat (Dometic MSH300), far less than a plug-in heater, so a salvaged pair can warm a chair from a battery. In the car a thermistor in the seat feeds a controller that regulates the heat (Autopian heated seat); a loose pad has no control of its own, so give it a fuse and a thermostat or timer. Dometic's rules for its seat pads: level 1 only for people who feel heat poorly, and no blankets or coats over a switched-on seat, so don't use one as a bed warmer under covers. A paraplegic driver was burned on the hip after about 30 minutes on high (Benjamin 2011).

sources.title: Dometic MSH300: Dometic (Waeco) MagicComfort MSH300/MSH301 seat heater, installation and operating manual (12 V, 10-70 W per seat)
